This miscellaneous appeal having been heard and reserv  orders, coming on for pronouncement this day, Justice Achal K  Paliwal pronounced the following:
ORDER This appeal by the Insurance Company under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is against the award dated 17.01.2020 passed by Member, MACT, Indore in Claim Case No.174/18.

By the aforesaid award, an amount of Rs.1,46,850/- has been awarded together with interest from the date of application till realization of the amount on account of the injuries sustained by the appellant/claimant in the accident occurred on 03.03.2015 and the Insurance Company has been held liable to pay the said amount of compensation.

2. Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company has submitted that as per the MLC report Ex.P/8, the accident in question occurred from a car but later on after nine days of the accident, an FIR was registered wherein it is stated that the accident has occurred from a motor cycle.
Thus, from the FIR registered by the claimant himself, it is apparent that it has been registered after a period of nine days and this delay has not been explained properly.
As the FIR Ex.P/2 has been filed by the claimant himself, therefore, the claimants are bound by the facts mentioned therein.

In support of the argument, counsel for the Insurance Company has relied upon a judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Premlata Shukla & others arising out of SLP (C)
No.2427/2006 (Civil Appeal No.2526/2007).

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Premlata Shukla & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, later on, motor cycle has been falsely involved in the accident.
It is further submitted that the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is excessive.

3. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents has submitted that at the time of MLC,
the claimant was not conscious, therefore, the claimant has not mentioned the fact of accident from the car in the MLC.
The claimant is illiterate.

The fact about the accident from the car has been National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Mahesh on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183922528/
2 mentioned on the basis of the information provided by the 108 Ambulance.

sentences.text: The Insurance Company has not examined the Investigating Officer and the Insurance Company has also not called the driver and owner in evidence and examined them.
Thus, there is no evidence to show that there is collusion between the claimant and the owner and driver of the motor cycle.

Learned counsel for the respondents has relied upon the judgment in the case of Manful and another vs. Mehmood and others reported in 2003 (4) MPLJ 174 and M.P State Road Transport Corporation vs. Vaijanti and others reported in 1995 ACJ 560.
4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: M.P State Road Transport Corporation vs. Vaijanti and others reported in 1995 ACJ 560
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

5. The submissions of the learned counsel for the appellant and grounds taken in the appeal memo reveal that the appellant/Insurance Company has challenged the impugned award primarily on the ground of delayed FIR and that the motor cycle has been falsely involved in the case, for the sake of compensation.

6. Therefore, question arises for consideration in this appeal is, as to what is the effect of the delayed FIR and whether from the evidence on record, it is proved that the motor cycle has been falsely involved in the case or not.

7. It is correct that the FIR Ex.P/2 has been registered on 12.03.2015 and accident occurred on 03.03.2015 but it is evident from the FIR itself that it has been registered after enquiry with respect to the Rojnamchasana No.228 dated 03.03.2015.
It is also evident from the record of the case that with respect to present accident, charge sheet Ex.P/1 has also been filed against the respondent/driver of the motor cycle after investigation.

However, the appellant/Insurance Company has not examined the Investigating Officer so as to show that if accident occurred from car, then, why did he file the charge sheet against the rider of the motor cycle.

There is also on record Ex.P/6 which shows that the owner of the motor cycle has informed the Investigating Officer that on the date of the accident motor cycle bearing registration No.MP-09-4323 was being ridden by Suresh and he informed him that the accident had occurred from the said motor cycle.

8. So far as the MLC Ex.P/8 is concerned, appellant/Insurance Company has not examined the concerned doctor who prepared the MLC and neither Insurance Company has examined the person driving the ambulance 108 who brought the injured/claimant to the hospital to show that as to who informed the doctor that accident has occurred from the car.
Further, in MLC Ex.P/8, it is not mentioned clearly that above fact was stated by the claimant/injured himself.

9. Therefore, in view of above discussion, in the considered opinion of this Court, from evidence on record, it is not established at all that actually accident took place from the car and the motor cycle has been falsely involved later on and this fact is also not established from the delayed FIR which has been registered after the Rojnamcha enquiry.

Hence, principle laid down in Premlata (supra)
does not help appellant in any way.
10.
I have also gone through the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.

In the considered opinion of this Court, the amount awarded by the Tribunal is not excessive and it appears to be just National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Mahesh on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183922528/
3 and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.
